newsitem.title: USA: US refiner picks up Brent in sleepy foreign trade.
newsitem.headline: US refiner picks up Brent in sleepy foreign trade.

text.p: A U.S. refiner picked up a Brent cargo Wednesday, the only confirmed trade of the benchmark crude, breaking up what was otherwise a sleepy day on the foreign crude scene, at least outside the North Sea.

Players differed in the interpretations of the subdued nature of the market, with some viewing it as transitional in an otherwise balanced market, and others seeing it as the beginning of a softer period in the U.S. crude import scene.
"Most of the June liftings have been scooped up and July hasn't started in earnest yet," said one trader explaining the light activity on Wednesday.
The Brent cargo for June 5-7 delivery was sold by a Wall Street player to a midcontinent trader at a 10 cents discount to July Brent, traders said.

The Latin scene appeared to be a lot softer than the North Sea, amid widespread talk Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol was not well pleased with bids that came in on Tuesday for its Cusiana cargo for June 17-18 loading traders said.

Bids were said to be coming in at $1.50 to $1.40 discount to July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing -- too far below the $1.23 under sale of the high-quality light sweet crude British Petroleum made to midcontinent player Clark on Monday.

Part of the problem with the fate of Ecopetrol's second Cusiana cargo of the month was the Caribbean market for available ships, which, according to some U.S. traders, is growing tighter and forcing the fob cargo price lower.

"This cargo is on the verge of being distressed," said one trader, who predicted Ecopetrol would have done well to accept one of the lower bids, and will be lucky if values do not slide even more before it closes the deal.
Shipping sources said that indeed shipping was tight in the Caribbean, pricing transportation costs at about $1.20 a barrel, versus about $0.95 a barrel during the same year-ago period.
In other Colombian action, the Vasconia tender scooped up by a European company last week at $3.60 under July/WTI fob was heard reoffered this week at $3.45 under.
The best bids were coming in at $3.50 under, but most sources said the European refiner should have no problem fetching the $3.45 it is seeking.
Some said that with Venezuelan Mesa now assessed at about $3.20 under July/WTI, Vasconia ought to fetch at least the $3.45 now on offer.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
